text: This essay argues that remote work increases employee productivity because it removes commute-related fatigue, gives workers control over their environment, and reduces office distractions, and each of these points is developed in the sections that follow.
Remote work is a thing that happens now and there are many opinions about it that people have.

A 2023 Stanford study of 16,000 workers found a 13% productivity gain among remote employees, and a separate Gallup survey reported a 24% drop in reported burnout, both of which directly support the claim that remote work improves output.
Everyone knows remote work is better because people say so all the time and it just makes sense if you think about it.
Governments should regulate social media platforms because unchecked algorithmic amplification of harmful content poses a measurable risk to public health and democratic discourse.
While free expression matters, social media companies' size and influence over public opinion now rival that of traditional media, and they should face comparable regulatory oversight.
Government regulation of social media is necessary specifically to address data privacy violations, even though content moderation should remain largely self-governed by platforms.
Social media should be regulated because it can be harmful to society.
There are many pros and cons to government regulation of social media, but overall it seems like a good idea.
Social media companies have too much power and something needs to change.
Social media is a big part of modern life and governments have been discussing what to do about it.
This essay will discuss social media regulation and look at different viewpoints.
Social media started in the early 2000s with platforms like Myspace and Friendster.
There are many different social media platforms that people use every day for different purposes.
Social media should be regulated to prevent misinformation, though the exact methods are unclear.
The government should step in because platforms have shown they can't moderate themselves effectively.
Some form of regulation is probably necessary, mainly to protect children from harmful content online.
Because social media companies profit from engagement-driven algorithms that spread misinformation, governments should regulate how those algorithms operate.
Data privacy abuses by social media platforms are widespread enough that stronger government regulation is justified.
Governments should regulate social media to curb the spread of harmful content aimed at minors.

A 2021 Facebook whistleblower report revealed the company's own research showed Instagram worsened body image issues in 32% of teen girls surveyed, and the platform continued running the algorithm anyway.

Studies from the Pew Research Center found that 64% of extremist recruitment contacts documented by researchers originated on unmoderated social platforms, directly linking lax oversight to real-world radicalization.
The EU's Digital Services Act, enacted in 2022, cut documented instances of illegal content on major platforms by a measurable margin within its first year, showing regulation can work in practice.
Research has shown that unregulated algorithmic feeds increase user engagement with divisive content, citing internal studies from major platforms themselves.
Several documented cases exist of foreign governments using social media ads to interfere in elections, which regulation could help prevent.
A study found that teens who spend more than three hours a day on social media report higher rates of anxiety and depression.
Studies show that social media can be harmful to mental health.
Many experts agree that regulation would help reduce the spread of misinformation online.
Research has found a connection between social media use and various social problems.
Everyone knows social media causes problems in society today.
It's obvious that these platforms need more oversight given everything that's happened.
People have been talking about this issue for a long time now.
Social media is used by billions of people around the world every single day.
I think social media regulation is an interesting topic to write about.
Twitter was founded in 2006 and has changed a lot each year.
